transcript: Yesterday, Paul and I saw Public Obscenities at Theater for a New Audience, a coproduction with Soho Rep where this piece originated last year. This is a big three hour play but the basic premise is that a Bengali American PhD student is visiting his home in India with his American boyfriend to do research. They're staying with an aunt and uncle and a couple other characters include a housekeeper, and some locals who are being interviewed about the queer experience in India. The number of plot points is almost excessive but it kind of results in an expansive and cinematic portrait that was to me more generally about family, identity, and culture. With so many different characters and interwoven stories, it feels somewhat slow, but not boring, more in a meditative sense. There's dialogue in English and Bangla which is often accompanied by English subtitles projected on the wall. Also projected on the wall are some very entertaining chat exchanges that one character has with someone online while they're playing online billiards together. As I reflect on the piece, I could have done with fewer loose ends and maybe a bit sharper of a progression in terms of plot but I found the performances captivating and I quite enjoyed the experience of the play. It was a good way to spend a Saturday afternoon. With that, another program for my collection.
